name: Bolaji Oki
summary: A rangy Belgian kickboxer (10-4 in our data, 3-3 counting his Contender Series win) who is dangerous early with a jab, leg kicks, body work and a heavy right hand. He drops to featherweight for this fight after losing three of his last four UFC bouts, all three losses by stoppage (guillotine, ground-and-pound, knockout).

how_they_fight.Striking: Long, busy kickboxing: jab up and down, outside leg kicks, body hooks, knees in the clinch and a right hand he likes to throw after dipping off the centre line (Cageside on the Aswell win). High output (136 significant strikes landed against Aswell in our data) and real power: he dropped Mason Jones early and stopped Dylan Salvador in round one on the Contender Series as an underdog.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Mostly a striker. He can scramble to top position and land hammerfists (he did after Sousa's kimura attempt) and holds a clinch well, but he does not chain takedowns, and when he is taken down by a committed wrestler he has not got back up reliably.
how_they_fight.Defense: Decent shell and head movement at range, and he caught Manoel Sousa coming in during round two. The holes: getting backed onto the fence (Sousa's KO), getting taken down and mounted (Jones), and a guillotine caught while he was winning the striking against Chris Duncan (28-10 in significant strikes per our data).
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Fast starter. Against Aswell he kept a high pace for 15 minutes, but against Jones he emptied the tank chasing a finish in round one and was flat and dominated in round two (Cageside). Of his six career finishes in our data, four came in round one, one in round two and one in round three; he has gone the distance five times (4-1). Stopped three times: round one (Duncan, submission), round two (Jones, elbows from mount) and round three (Sousa, punch at 4:12 in our data).
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Composed against volume strikers and willing to show new looks (spinning backfist into head kick vs Aswell), but in his losses he has spent energy recklessly when he smells a finish and kept fighting near the fence late. Coverage of the Jones loss flagged cardio and fight IQ as concerns.

patterns: Front-loads his offence: four of six career finishes came in round one
Jab to the body, outside leg kicks, right hand off a dip
Lost three of his last four UFC fights, all inside the distance (R1 sub, R2 TKO, R3 KO)
Late damage: buckled at the end of R2 and knocked out in the last minute of R3 against Sousa
concerns: First UFC fight at 145 after competing at 155; cut and power at the new weight are unknowns
Chin and durability: dropped by Sousa in R1 and finished in R3
Fades after a big first-round effort (Jones)
Takedown defense against a determined wrestler
keys_to_beat: Survive his first-round power, then push the pace into rounds two and three
Pressure him to the fence and land the right hand
Take him down after he has spent energy and work from top position
Make him grapple; he has been submitted and stopped from mount

news.text: Made weight at the official weigh-ins: 146 lb (Santos 146). First featherweight cut done.
Sherdog preview: +100 underdog (Santos -120); sees his size as an edge if he wrestles but doubts his defence under a high pace; picks Santos by second-round stoppage.
UFC.com Fight By Fight Preview expects an early Fight of the Night contender.
Booked against Daniel Santos on the UFC 333 prelims; Oki moves down to featherweight for the bout.
Knocked out by debuting Manoel Sousa at 4:12 of round three (our data; Cageside lists 4:14), his second straight stoppage loss.
Per BJPenn.com, he withdrew injured from a February 2025 booking against Mohammad Al-Selwady.
